analysis.evidence: אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ identifies the speakers as addressing one another. Their words begin with הָבָה נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים, “Come, let us make bricks.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks the Qal wayyiqtol. The י־ prefix and ־וּ ending mark the third person masculine plural.

analysis.evidence: After the plural וַיֹּאמְרוּ ‘they said’, אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ means ‘each to his fellow’. אִישׁ singles out each speaker in the reciprocal exchange.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, used distributively.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ, “they said to one another,” אֶל introduces רֵעֵהוּ, the fellow whom each speaker addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After the plural וַיֹּאמְרוּ ‘they said’, אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ means ‘each to his fellow’. The clause reads ‘they said to one another’.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.
analysis.sense: the other in the reciprocal expression אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ

draft.change: Add the exhortative sense come-now to the Hebrew Qal of יָהַב.
draft.definition: The imperative הָבָה introduces a proposal and urges the hearer to act with the speaker.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 11:3, הָבָה introduces נִלְבְּנָה, “let us make bricks,” followed by וְנִשְׂרְפָה, “and let us burn them.” Both cohortatives express the shared undertaking.

analysis.evidence: Each says to his fellow הָבָה נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים, “Come now, let us make bricks.” The first-person plural cohortative נִלְבְּנָה states the proposal that הָבָה introduces. לְבֵנִים names what they propose to make.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second-person masculine singular, with paragogic ה. Each speaker addresses his fellow, then includes himself in the proposed action.
analysis.sense: Urge the hearer to join the speaker in a proposed action.

analysis.evidence: הָבָה introduces a proposal, and לְבֵנִים supplies the cognate object “bricks.” The following verb וְנִשְׂרְפָה describes firing the bricks after they are formed.
analysis.morphology: Qal first-person common plural cohortative. The initial נִ־ marks the first-person plural, and the final ־ָה marks the cohortative.

analysis.evidence: In נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים, “let us make bricks,” the noun is the object of the related verb נִלְבְּנָה. The speakers propose firing the bricks, and the verse then says that brick served them as stone.
analysis.morphology: Feminine common noun in the plural absolute, with the plural ending ־ִים. The initial ל is part of the stem.

analysis.evidence: The speakers first propose making לְבֵנִים, “bricks,” which supplies the implied object of וְנִשְׂרְפָה. The following cognate noun לִשְׂרֵפָה emphasizes the firing, and the verse says the resulting brick served as stone.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins a Qal first-person common plural cohortative to the preceding cohortative נִלְבְּנָה. The prefix נִ־ marks the first person plural, and the ending ־ָה marks the cohortative.

analysis.evidence: The builders propose making לְבֵנִים ‘bricks’. The phrase וְנִשְׂרְפָה לִשְׂרֵפָה pairs ‘let us burn’ with the noun from the same root, giving the sense ‘let us fire them thoroughly’.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ־ precedes a feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: A burning, here the firing of bricks in their manufacture.

analysis.evidence: לָהֶם identifies the builders for whom the brick served, and לְאָבֶן gives its function: they used brick as stone. The parallel clause describes their use of bitumen as mortar.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed וַ followed by the Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, agreeing with הַלְּבֵנָה, “the brick.”

analysis.evidence: הַלְּבֵנָה refers back to the לְבֵנִים they proposed to make and fire. The singular names the building material that served them as stone (לְאָבֶן).
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial ל of the feminine singular absolute noun לְבֵנָה.

analysis.evidence: The builders fired bricks, and הַלְּבֵנָה לְאָבֶן says that brick served them as building stone, just as bitumen served them as mortar in the parallel clause.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks the role the brick served. אָבֶן is the pausal form of the feminine singular absolute noun אֶבֶן.

analysis.evidence: The verse says that brick served as stone and that הַחֵמָר served לָהֶם לַחֹמֶר, “as mortar for them.” The marked noun חֵמָר names the material, bitumen. The final noun חֹמֶר names its use as mortar.
analysis.morphology: וְ is the conjunction “and,” הַ is the definite article, and חֵמָר is a masculine singular noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: לָהֶם identifies the builders for whom the bitumen served, and לַחֹמֶר identifies its use as mortar. The preceding clause gives the parallel use of brick as stone.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third-person masculine singular, agreeing with הַחֵמָר “the bitumen.”
